title: Resilient dedicated pools: zone prioritization and sovereignty enforcement
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Dedicated customers increasingly require both deterministic throughput guarantees and strict data locality controls. We currently support simple pool affinity and regional placement but lack a compact policy layer that enforces per-customer residency constraints while allowing graceful zone failover and strictly bounded throughput degradation. Goals: 1) Allow operators/tenants to declare an ordered list of preferred zones (priority list) and a set of allowed sovereignty regions. 2) Map each dedicated pool to a placement policy that ensures throughput SLOs are maintained under normal and degraded conditions via reserved capacity, controlled autoscaler knobs, and soft-drain workflows. 3) Enforce data sovereignty at scheduling and runtime by tagging KV caches, logs, and audit trails; provide strong visibility for audits. 4) Provide operational tooling for controlled failover (safe fanout limits, rolling failover, and rapid rollback) and telemetry to measure compliance and cost impact.
proposal: Implement a Placement Policy abstraction and a Placement Controller in the control plane. Key components: - Policy model: priority_zones (ordered), allowed_regions, min_reserved_qps, failover_mode (soft|hard), max_failover_fanout, prefer_local_kv_cache (bool). - Scheduler changes: respect ordered preferences, only place replicas/allocations in allowed_regions; use min_reserved_qps to pre-allocate capacity on placement. - Autoscaler: new policy-driven autoscaler that treats min_reserved_qps as floor capacity and enforces scale-out rate limits; supports burst windows and cost-aware fallback to quantized model variants. - Runtime tagging: all requests, KV caches, and persisted traces for this customer include locality tags; enforcement hooks to prevent cross-region persistence. - Failover flow: controlled three-step process: 1) notify affected pool, 2) pre-warm fallback zone(s) to min_reserved_qps, 3) drain with soft-shed policies to avoid thundering scale-ups. - Observability: add per-customer residency compliance metric, failover latency, throughput shortfall, and estimated cost delta.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Admin can create a Placement Policy with priority_zones and allowed_regions via Console and API.
2) Allocations for dedicated pools respect the policy: no allocation is scheduled outside allowed_regions.
3) Under single-zone outage scenario, placement controller fails over to next preferred zone within configured max_failover_fanout and maintains >= min_reserved_qps for 95% of tenanted requests within the SLO window.
4) Autoscaler honors min_reserved_qps as floor and applies configured scale-out rate limits; observed token-cost does not exceed predicted model by >10% in steady state.
5) All persisted artifacts for policy-bound pools include locality tags and appear in audit logs; an audit query returns no cross-region persisted records for customers with strict sovereignty.
6) Playbook for controlled failover documented and validated in a staged runbook with on-call and SEs; rollback tested.
7) End-to-end integration tests (simulated zone fail, prewarm, drain) pass in CI with deterministic outcomes.
risks:
- Risk of capacity fragmentation if many tenants use strict min_reserved_qps; could reduce cluster efficiency.
- Failure to pre-warm fallback zones could cause transient SLA breaches.
- Incorrect tagging/enforcement could lead to residency violations with regulatory consequences.
- Autoscaler complexity could introduce oscillations if not rate-limited.
mitigations:
- Introduce bin-packing heuristics and a marketplace of soft vs hard reservations; recommend pooled reservations for small tenants.
- Prewarm circuit: require prewarm success checks and fallback to degraded-mode with clear customer notifications.
- Add unit tests and end-to-end audits for locality tags; require security review and automated policy compliance gating before production rollout.
- Autoscaler will implement exponential backoff and a global damping factor to reduce oscillation; include canary rollout in Dedicated clusters.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): implement Placement Policy model and controller; enable for internal test tenants and 3 pilot customers with non-strict sovereignty. Phase 2: autoscaler integration and prewarm logic; run closed beta with 10 customers (mix of P0/P1). Phase 3: enable full Console UI, audit queries, and sign off security review. Phase 4: wide release with migration tooling to convert existing pools to policies and a cost-estimation tool for customers. Each phase gated by compliance tests and SLOs.
telemetry_and_metrics: Metrics to add: residency_compliance_rate, failover_time_p50/p95/p99, min_reserved_qps_violations_per_hour, throughput_shortfall_pct, prewarm_success_rate, failover_fanout_count, cost_delta_estimate. Dashboards: per-tenant residency dashboard and fleet-level heatmap for policy-induced fragmentation.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for policy parser, scheduling predicates, and local enforcement hooks.
- Integration tests in staging that simulate zone latency and full zone drain.
- Load tests to validate throughput guarantees under mixed workloads.
- Compliance test that attempts cross-region persistence and must be blocked for strict policies.
migration_notes:
- Provide migration script to convert existing 'preferred_zones' free-text into structured Placement Policies.
- Offer a grace window where autoscaler runs in advisory mode for 2 weeks to let customers observe cost/availability impact before hard enforcement.
- Provide support bundle that lists estimated capacity fragmentation and suggested mitigation (pooled reservations or adjusting min_reserved_qps).
operational_playbook:
- On single-zone failure: Trigger Placement Controller failover runbook; coordinate with on-call to prewarm fallback zones and monitor prewarm_success_rate.
- If prewarm fails: execute degraded-mode notification (throttle non-critical tenants) and open ticket with infra team.
- Post-mortem: collect residency_compliance_rate and throughput_shortfall_pct; run root cause and update policy defaults.
